title: Principalizing a supported ideal on an etale scheme by modifying its base
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $D\hookrightarrow S$ be an effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and put $U=S\setminus|D|$. Assume $U$ is quasi-compact and schematically dense, meaning $\mathcal O_S\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. Let $e:V\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_V$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] whose restriction to $e^{-1}U$ is $\mathcal O_{e^{-1}U}$. There exists a $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1\to S$ (the blowup of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal equal to the unit ideal on $U$) [def-nagata-admissible-blowup, def-nagata-global-blowup] such that the extended ideal $\mathcal K\mathcal O_{V\times_S S_1}\subseteq\mathcal O_{V\times_S S_1}$ is invertible [def-nagata-invertible-ideal]; equivalently, it is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. The fibre product and extended ideal are those of [def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-extended-ideal]. No Noetherian or excellence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0815 (theorem-flatten-module), applied to an ideal on an etale scheme; the identification of the module strict transform with the extended ideal and its rank-one consequence are the additional comparison asserted here. Reconstructs the finite-stage principalization input implicit in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.373.

proof.text: On e^{-1}U the ideal inclusion is an isomorphism: on affine opens its image is the unit ideal and the inclusion is injective. Restriction therefore identifies K.toModules with the structure module. The latter is finitely presented. At x in this open the induced stalk inclusion is an isomorphism to O_{V,x}; restrict scalars along e.stalkMap x, whose ring map is flat because e is etale. These give both open hypotheses of the flattening theorem. Apply that theorem to obtain the admissible centre B, its finite-type ideal and a finitely presented relatively flat strict transform.

Use the flat-ideal strict-transform comparison for e and B.I. Apply the module stalk functor and restriction of scalars to the resulting isomorphism to transfer the relative stalk-flatness to the extended ideal L=K.comap p. Finite presentation transfers along the same isomorphism.

The boundary D.comap B.I.blowupMap is Cartier by preservation of Cartier ideals under blowups. The pullback square gives e∘p=b∘g, and support_comap identifies the complementary open with g^{-1}b^{-1}U. Restricting p to that open factors through e^{-1}U, so functoriality of ideal comap and the original unit restriction imply that L is the unit ideal there.

The projection g is etale, quasi-compact and separated by base change. Apply the rank-one criterion to g, the pulled-back Cartier boundary and L, using the finite presentation, relative flatness and unit restriction already proved. This yields the required invertibility for the same blowup B.

tool_uses.why: The general module flattening theorem provides the base blowup and a finitely presented relatively flat transform; the perverse unit contains no such geometric theorem.
Preservation of an effective Cartier divisor under an arbitrary blowup supplies the regular boundary equation; it is a generic geometric tool absent from the perverse unit.
Relative flatness over a Cartier boundary supplies injectivity of restriction for the structure sheaf; no perverse-unit statement supplies this torsion calculation.
The general epimorphism from tensor pullback to extended ideal identifies the actual image ideal, rather than assuming that base change preserves the inclusion.
The generic complement-of-centre isomorphism proves that the kernel is supported on the exceptional locus.
The general description of etale fibres makes their local rings fields, supplying fibre flatness for the freeness criterion.
The general relative-flatness plus fibre-flatness criterion upgrades the finitely presented transform to a locally free module; no perverse-unit statement does so.
